title: ‘Women Academics’ Perceptions of Women’s leadership in a South African Higher Education institution
journal: International Journal of Studies in Psychology
abstract: Although women make up a larger share of the academic workforce, their representation in top leadership positions such as deans, deputy vice-chancellors, and vice-chancellors remains disproportionately low. The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5, which promotes women’s full and effective involvement in leadership and decision-making, is threatened by this ongoing imbalance. This study explored women academics’ perceptions regarding women's leadership in a South African higher education institution. It used a qualitative approach through an exploratory qualitative research design. Twenty female academics were purposively selected from a Semi-metropolitan institution in Limpopo for this study. Semi-structured interviews were used to gather data from black African women in academia, ranging from junior lecturers to associate professors. Thematic analysis was employed to analyse the data. The findings revealed eight themes: Lower self-esteem amongst women, Men perceived as more capable than women, Competitive desire, Failure to meet requirements, Lack of support, Marginalisation fear, Patriarchal institutions, and Societal stereotypes. The underrepresentation of women in leadership positions results from several factors combined. The study concludes that institutional change, improved mentorship programmes, inclusive leadership development programmes, and the dismantling of patriarchal norms that still limit women’s leadership opportunities in academia are necessary to achieve gender equity in higher education leadership. The findings of this study hold significant consequences for policy and practice within higher education institutions. The ongoing existence of women’s reduced self-esteem, views of men as more competent leaders, and the dominance of patriarchal institutional cultures indicate that gender disparities in leadership are not just personal obstacles but are ingrained in organisational frameworks and practices.

title: Türkçe ve Türk kültürü ders kitaplarındaki okuma metinlerinde matematiksel dilin incelenmesi
abstract: Bu araştırmanın amacı, Millî Eğitim Bakanlığı tarafından yayımlanan Türkçe ve Türk Kültürü (5-8. seviye) ders kitaplarındaki okuma metinlerinde yer alan matematiksel dil unsurlarını belirlemek ve bu unsurların belirlenen matematiksel alanlara göre dağılımını incelemektir. Nitel araştırma yöntemlerinden doküman incelemesiyle tasarlanan çalışmanın veri setini, toplam 64 okuma metni oluşturmaktadır. Verilerin analizinde, Türkiye Yüzyılı Maarif Modeli İlkokul Matematik Dersi Öğretim Programları (2024 ve 2026) referans alınarak dört ana kategoriden oluşan betimsel bir analiz çerçevesi kullanılmıştır. Araştırma sonuçları, matematiksel dilin ağırlıklı olarak Sayılar ve Nicelik Algısı ile Geometri ve Uzamsal İlişkiler kategorilerinde yoğunlaştığını; İşlemler ve Cebirsel Düşünme ile Veri, Araştırma ve Olasılık alanlarının ise sınırlı temsil edildiğini göstermiştir. Metinlerdeki matematiksel dil unsurlarının, Türkçe ve Türk Kültürü Dersi Öğretim Programı’ndaki (2026) karşılaştırma, gerekçelendirme ve sıralama öğrenme çıktılarıyla kavramsal paralellik taşıdığı ve bu ilişkinin özellikle 7. seviyede belirginleştiği tespit edilmiştir. Elde edilen bulgular, metinlerde yer verilen somut ve bağlamsal ifadelerin iki dilli öğrencilerin matematiksel söz varlığını destekleme olanağı sağladığına ve Türkçe öğretiminde okuduğunu anlama becerilerine katkı sunabileceğine işaret etmektedir. This study aims to identify the elements of mathematical language in the reading texts of Turkish and Turkish Culture textbooks (levels 5-8) published by the Ministry of National Education and to analyze their distribution across specified mathematical domains. Designed within the qualitative research paradigm using document analysis, the study's dataset comprises a total of 64 reading texts. A descriptive analysis framework consisting of four main categories—developed with reference to the Primary School Mathematics Curriculum of the Century of Türkiye Education Model—was utilized for data analysis. The findings revealed that mathematical language was predominantly concentrated in the categories of Numbers and Quantity Perception and Geometry and Spatial Relations, whereas Operations and Algebraic Thinking and Data, Research, and Probability were represented to a limited extent. It was determined that the mathematical language elements in the texts share conceptual parallels with the learning outcomes of comparison, justification, and sequencing in the Turkish and Turkish Culture Curricula (2024 and 2026), a relationship that becomes particularly pronounced at the 7th level. The findings suggest that concrete and contextual expressions used in the texts may enhance the mathematical vocabulary of bilingual students and could serve an interdisciplinary function that supports reading comprehension skills in Turkish language instruction.

title: Trends in rheumatic heart disease mortality in the United States of America from 1968 to 2023: a nationwide analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is a preventable sequela of acute rheumatic fever causing chronic valvular damage to the heart. In the United States of America (USA), RHD persists among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. This study examines long-term trends in RHD mortality from 1968 to 2023, identifying associated demographic and geographic factors to guide targeted public health interventions. Methods This retrospective observational study examined death certificate data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (WONDER) database, encompassing three different International Classification of Disease periods (ICD-8, ICD-9, ICD-10). Analysis included stratification by age, gender, race, ethnicity and urbanisation level. Joinpoint analysis and multiple regression analysis were used to identify trends. Results RHD mortality declined significantly from 1968 to 2012, with falling crude mortality rates in both sexes and large reductions in absolute deaths among White individuals and adults aged 55–74 years. From 2012 to 2023, total deaths increased from 3,083 to 4,332, crude mortality rose from 0.98 to 1.29 per 100,000 and age-adjusted mortality increased from 0.88 to 1.04 per 100,000 (all p < 0.0001). Increases were observed across sex, race, ethnicity, urbanisation, and most age subgroups. Females had consistently higher RHD crude mortality rate ratios than men (1.09–2.43). The age distribution of RHD mortality shifted markedly over the study period, with deaths among individuals aged ≥ 75 years increasing from 17% in 1968 to 61% in 2023. Race- and ethnicity-specific CMR increased across all assessed groups from 2012 to 2023, with the largest relative increases among American Indian or Alaska Native individuals (+ 112.4%; β = 0.033 per 100,000/year, p = 0.002) and Hispanic individuals (+ 60.2%; β = 0.014 per 100,000/year, p < 0.001). Conclusion Following decades of decline, RHD mortality in the United States increased after 2012. Our study identified a persistent female predominance in RHD mortality and a marked shift in mortality burden from middle-aged adults towards older populations.

title: Solar tunnel dryer and slice thickness effect on the chemical composition and functional properties of taro corms flour
Scheduled versus on-demand nonopioid analgesia after cesarean delivery under regional anesthesia: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
abstract: Effective pain relief after cesarean delivery is crucial for maternal comfort, recovery, and breastfeeding. Although scheduled nonopioid analgesics are standard, on-demand regimens have been suggested to reduce drug exposure. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL were systematically searched from inception to August 20, 2025, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing scheduled vs. on-demand nonopioid analgesia following cesarean delivery under regional anesthesia. The primary outcomes were postoperative pain intensity and analgesic consumption, and the secondary outcomes were maternal satisfaction, adverse effects, breastfeeding outcomes, and neonatal safety. Three RCTs that included 666 women were identified. At 24 h, scheduled dosing significantly reduced pain scores compared with on-demand regimens (mean difference [MD] 0.98, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55 to 1.41; P < 0.001, I2 = 78%), but no difference was observed at 48 h (MD 0.76, 95% CI –0.30 to 1.82; P = 0.16, I2 = 96%). Overall analgesic consumption did not differ significantly between groups (standardized MD –0.23, 95% CI –0.62 to 0.16, P = 0.24; I2 = 80%). Maternal adverse effects were rare and similar across groups (risk difference −0.01, 95% CI −0.04 to 0.02; I2 = 0%). Breastfeeding outcomes were inconsistently defined, with two trials indicating benefits from scheduled dosing. Neonatal safety outcomes were reported in one trial, showing no differences between groups. Scheduled nonopioid analgesia after cesarean delivery under regional anesthesia was linked to better pain control during the first postoperative day. After this period, the comparative effectiveness of scheduled vs. on-demand regimens remained uncertain, with considerable variability across studies. No significant differences were found in analgesic consumption or maternal adverse effects, and evidence regarding breastfeeding and neonatal outcomes was limited.

title: Pemulihan Restoring the Function of 30 Lecture Hall Seats by Fixing Used Furniture on Campus
abstract: This project aimed to restore the function of 30 lecture chairs with integrated writing desks at Manado State Polytechnic. Progress reports and notes K01–K30 were analyzed to categorize damages, actions, and results of function inspections. Work from June 8 to September 28, 2026, recorded the replacement of upholstery on all units; 21 units had seat upholstery issues and 17 units had backrest upholstery issues, with eight units having both. Thirteen actions were recorded in June, five in July, four in August, and eight in September. All 30 units showed positive function results. Findings indicate 100% coverage on physical actions, while program reports showed 80% progress. Signed test sheets, cost data, and placement evidence provided a standard safety assessment and utilization impact
